hypothesis_title: Thalamocortical Coupling and Default Mode Network Dysregulation Interaction in Insomnia
scientific_question: How do sleep disturbances (ISI, PSQI) relate to brain connectivity (fMRI features) and psychological factors (BAI, BDI) in a novel analysis framework?
hypothesis_summary: Sleep disruption in insomnia may involve a bidirectional interaction between thalamocortical coupling deficits and default mode network (DMN) dysregulation, exacerbating cognitive and emotional symptoms.
hypothesis_content: Insomnia severity is associated with both reduced thalamocortical coupling (thalamus_DMN_FC) and DMN dysregulation (DMN_FC), which may synergistically impair task execution, decision-making, and self-referential processing. Targeted interventions addressing both mechanisms could improve sleep outcomes.

primary_tests.question: Does thalamus_DMN_FC explain variation in ISI?
Does DMN_FC explain variation in ISI?
Does timefreq_fALFF_0.01_0.08_over_0.01_0.25 explain variation in ISI?
Does timefreq_ALFF_0.01_0.08 explain variation in ISI?

analysis_plan: Measure thalamocortical coupling (EEG-fMRI) and DMN functional connectivity (fMRI) in insomnia patients (ISI ≥ 10) and controls. Correlate thalamus_DMN_FC and DMN_FC with ISI scores, controlling for AHI and sleep efficiency. Test for interaction effects between thalamocortical coupling and DMN dysregulation on cognitive performance metrics.

llm_experiment_design.scientific_question: How do sleep disturbances (ISI, PSQI) relate to brain connectivity (fMRI features) and psychological factors (BAI, BDI) in a novel analysis framework?

primary_tests.hypothesis: Thalamus-DMN functional connectivity (thalamus_DMN_FC) predicts insomnia severity (ISI) after controlling for BAI and BDI
DMN functional connectivity (DMN_FC) correlates with sleep quality (PSQI) independent of age and education

secondary_tests.hypothesis: Amygdala-DMN connectivity (amygdala_DMN_FC) mediates the relationship between BDI and PSQI

risk_mitigation.multiple_testing: Bonferroni correction applied across all primary tests
risk_mitigation.confounding: Covariate selection based on prior literature (age, education, BAI/BDI as psychological controls)

llm_experiment_design.rationale: Focuses on untested fMRI-PSQI relationships while leveraging psychological scales as covariates. Avoids prior signatures by targeting novel connectivity metrics (amygdala-DMN) and sleep outcomes (PSQI).
